overall: Los Angeles is finishing a mild June day with a running maximum of 72.0°F, already achieved around 15:07 ET and holding through 17:00 ET. Temperatures are now clearly in decline — down to 69.8°F by 18:52 ET with a cooling velocity of -1.8°F/hr and accelerating at -3.6°F/hr over the last 30 minutes. Patchy fog is moving in for the evening, reinforcing the cooling trend and making any recovery essentially impossible.
forecast_obs_notes: All NWP models underforecast today's actual high: ECMWF came in at 68.5°F, NBM at 67.0°F, and even the warmest model (HRRR at 71.3°F) fell short of the observed 72.0°F running max. The NWS text forecast of 'near 70°F' was also beaten, suggesting a marine-layer clearing event allowed slightly more afternoon heating than anticipated before onshore flow and fog reasserted.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is almost certainly already locked in at 72.0°F — the peak occurred roughly 3.7 hours ago and temperatures are on a firm downward trajectory with no realistic path to recovery given the hour, accelerating cooling, and incoming fog. The META model's top bucket of 74–75°F (44.7%) now appears too warm given observed data; the 72–73°F bucket is the effective floor and likely the final answer. Confidence is very high that TMAX lands right at or just above 72°F.
